How do I apply for enrollment for a new child?

Upon getting to the bottom of the page, you will be presented with the following screen. Parents that are registering their students for the Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program or Texas Tech K-12 Full-Time Diploma program should select the "Texas Tech K-12 Intake Form".

Following the Form Type selection, pressing the "Begin" button will take you to the next page to select the program that you are interested in signing your student up for. As Texas Tech K-12 continues to expand, we are pleased to offer the following programs:

Supplemental Individual Student (Part-Time) (opens in new tab)

If you remain enrolled at your local school and want to take a Texas Tech K-12 course to graduate early or on time, take courses not offered at your local school, make up failed credits, or have an alternative for summer school, you will select the Supplemental/Part-time option. Students must receive prior approval from their school counselor before enrolling in any course or Credit By Exam. Failure to obtain approval may result in unawarded credit for a course or Credit By Exam.

How do I access my final course grade?

Final course grades will be posted to the student's Focus account under "Grades".

Please note the following:

· Full-Time Texas Tech K-12 Students: A final grade will be recorded on his/her official Texas Tech K-12 transcript as well as posted in the student's portal. Full-time students may request a copy of their transcript from inside of Focus, or via the transcript request (opens in new tab).

· Non Full-Time Texas Tech K-12 Students: Students and parents may view the final course grade on the portal. It is the student’s responsibility to very that the grade is received and recorded on their official school transcript.

· Homeschool Students: Final grades may be viewed on the portal. Grade Reports may be printed from the portal.

· We have received some reports of School Counselors and students not being able to access the Adobe PDF copy of the grade report. We ask that you please ensure that you are using Google Chrome and that in your extensions, that the Adobe Acrobat extension is currently enabled. We also ask that you please ensure that your current Adobe setting is set to “Covert Current web page to an Adobe PDF File has access to this site. If these settings are not enabled, we ask that you please check with your School or District IT to ensure that the extensions are enabled.

Benefits of the Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program

Step 1: Allow students to start with Texas Tech K-12 at anytime

Step 2: From the date of enrollment, students have six months (180 days) to complete the course

Step 3: Complete final exams from home with Texas Tech K-12’s proctoring service, Proctorio.

Step 4: Graduate Early or On Time: Stay on track—or get ahead—with courses that complement your current school curriculum.

Step 5: Access Advanced Placement (AP) Courses: Challenge yourself with college-level coursework that prepares you for higher education and boosts your college applications.

Step 6: Expand Your Learning Options: Enroll in courses not available at traditional schools to broaden your academic experience.

Step 7: Learn on Your Schedule: Our self-paced format fits seamlessly with your existing school schedule and commitments.

Step 8: Recover Credits: Retake courses to make up failed credits and stay on track for graduation.

Step 9: Replace Summer School: Complete required coursework during the summer without a traditional classroom setting.

Attendance/Progress Requirements

Step 1: In your all-online program, attendance “will” be defined as progress within each semester course.

Step 2: You will have six months to complete each semester course.

Step 3: You must maintain enrollment in a minimum of four semester courses.

Step 4: You must make weekly progress in each course by working in each course a minimum of three days per 7-day period.

Step 5: You must complete a minimum of 5% of course assignments in every seven-day period. For example, if your course has 20 assignments, you need to complete a minimum of one per week. If your course has 60 assignments, you must average a minimum of three per week.

Please note:

Step 1: Completing the minimum number of assignments does not guaranteed you will complete within the 6-month time frame.

Step 2: Completing the minimum number of assignments and courses may not maintain your appropriate grade level or anticipated graduation date.

Step 3: If your progress is adequate, your parent may request “vacation” days.

Step 4: Extensions are not available, so you must schedule your weekly progress to complete the minimum of four courses during the 6-month period.

Step 5: Failure to meet minimum progress requirements may cause Texas Tech K-12 to implement truancy processes and may result in your removal from the program.

Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exam's excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessment and Academic Readiness (STAAR) EOC (End of Course) exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

In addition to working towards a high school diploma, you may request a Verification Of Enrollment and Student ID (opens in new tab) cards. You may also participate in PSAT, ACT, AND SAT exams.

Supplemental Program Information

Anyone looking to supplement their current school curriculum or home school curriculum can enroll in Texas Tech K-12.  Our Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) is designed to allow students in elementary, middle and high school that allows students to work at their own pace. We have students who must do their work at home for various reasons, such as travel "outside" of the U.S. for extended amounts of time, have health issues, are actors, entertainers, and athletes who cannot fit the traditional schooling into their schedule. We have school all year and do not keep a traditional academic schedule, so it is possible to move through our program faster than the typical semester-based programs.

This is a self-paced program where all the instructional content is provided. The courses tend to be reading and writing intensive. Online courses require self-discipline and excellent time-management skills. The courses are not virtual classrooms and do not require any interaction with any other students or instructors. Each course has lessons, which are like chapters, and a final exam. The final exam will be proctored online by an online proctoring service.

WHAT HAPPENS IF I CANNOT BE THERE TO TEST?

If you are ill or have an emergency, please contact your testing coordinator immediately. To ensure that you remain on schedule to graduate, participation in and successful completion of both State of Texas Assessment of Academic Readiness and State of Texas Assessment of Academic Readiness/End Of Course is necessary and is a condition of your enrollment with Texas Tech K-12. Failure to test will result in removal from the tuition-free program per our attendance policy.

Identification Cards and Verification of Enrollment (VOE)

As a full-time student, you are eligible to receive a Texas Tech K-12 student identification card and Verification of Attendance (VOE).

If you are a full-time student who wishes to receive a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) for any purpose, including a driver’s permit, Social Security benefits or child support, avoiding truancy in your local district, or legal documentation of enrollment in a Texas Tech K-12 full-time program, you MUST meet the full-time student eligibility requirements as outlined above.

Students demonstrate attendance in Texas Tech K-12 online school by regularly completing assignments. Attendance is directly tied to what the student accomplishes and/or produces over a given period. Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exam's excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessment and Academic Readiness (STAAR) EOC (End of Course) exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

If an instructor suspects that an assignment is not the work of the student, it will receive a score of zero. **Proctoring for Online Credit-by-Exam**

- **Proctoring Tool**: Texas Tech K-12 uses Proctorio, an online proctoring service, for all online Credit-by-Exams. This service allows students to take exams remotely without needing a physical proctor.

  - **Browser**: Google Chrome is required, and the Proctorio extension must be installed.
  - **Device**: A desktop or laptop with a webcam and microphone is necessary. Mobile devices like phones and tablets are not supported.
  - **Internet**: A stable broadband connection with at least 1.5 Mbps is recommended.

  - **System Check**: Run the Proctorio system check to ensure compatibility.
  - **ID Verification**: Have a valid photo ID ready to show before the exam starts. Acceptable IDs include a state ID, driver's license, school ID, passport, or a yearbook photo with a name.
  - **Environment**: Ensure a quiet, well-lit room for the exam to avoid disruptions.

- **Exam Day**:
  - **Setup**: Log in using Google Chrome, ensure the Proctorio extension is active, and follow the prompts for ID verification and environment setup.
  - **Monitoring**: Proctorio will monitor video, audio, and screen activity during the exam.

The curriculum blends Texas Tech K-12 courses with dual credit options, designed to challenge and inspire. Courses offered through dual credit are self-paced (opens in new tab), allowing students to progress at their own speed and take control of their academic journey.

Supplemental Program Information

Anyone looking to supplement their current school curriculum or home school curriculum can enroll in Texas Tech K-12.  Our Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) is designed to allow students in elementary, middle and high school that allows students to work at their own pace. We have students who must do their work at home for various reasons, such as travel "outside" of the U.S. for extended amounts of time, have health issues, are actors, entertainers, and athletes who cannot fit the traditional schooling into their schedule. We have school all year and do not keep a traditional academic schedule, so it is possible to move through our program faster than the typical semester-based programs.

This is a self-paced program where all the instructional content is provided. The courses tend to be reading and writing intensive. Online courses require self-discipline and excellent time-management skills. The courses are not virtual classrooms and do not require any interaction with any other students or instructors. Each course has lessons, which are like chapters, and a final exam. The final exam will be proctored online by an online proctoring service.

When may I enroll?

Texas Tech K-12 does not operate on a semester basis; therefore, courses are asynchronous. Open enrollment allows you to enroll in any course, at any time, and work at your own pace. If you are enrolled in another district, obtain approval from your school counselor before enrolling in a course to ensure credit upon successful completion.

Supplemental Individual Student (Part-Time)

If you remain enrolled at your local school and want to take a Texas Tech K-12 course to graduate early or on time, take courses not offered at your local school, make up failed credits, or have an alternative for summer school; you will select the Supplemental/Part-time option. Students must receive prior approval from their school counselor before enrolling in any course or Credit By Exam (CBE). Failure to obtain approval may result in unawarded credit for a course or Credit By Exam. Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exam's excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessment and Academic Readiness (STAAR) EOC (End of Course) exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

In addition to working towards a high school diploma, you may request a Verification Of Enrollment and Student ID (opens in new tab) cards. You may also participate in PSAT, ACT, AND SAT exams.
